name: Costa Rica Rivense Chirripo Black Honey Geisha
altitude: 1700 masl tasting notes : hibiscus, red apple, honey about the coffee : Geisha from Café Rivense, a family-run farm and micromill in the Chirripó micro-region at 1,700 MASL. The black honey process — where most of the fruit mucilage is left on during drying — pushes the sweetness forward without muddying the varietal clarity. What you get is hibiscus and red apple up front, a clean honey sweetness through the mid, and a finish that lingers longer than you'd expect. Delicate but not shy

name: El Salvador Los Pirineos Orange Pacamara Washed
altitude: 1600 masl tasting notes : orange blossom, grapes, apricot about the coffee : Orange Pacamara is a large-bean mutation of Pacamara selected for its fruit-forward character, and Los Pirineos on the Tecapa volcano in Usulután is one of the farms that does it best. This lot delivers orange blossom and apricot upfront, with a grape-like sweetness that lingers. The washed process keeps it clean and precise. Light-roasted for filter. Floral, fruit-driven, and structured

name: Ethiopia Abdo Abamecha G1 Badeyi Lot 11
taste_notes: white floral, stone fruit, black tea
altitude: 2200 masl tasting notes : white floral, stone fruit, black tea about the coffee : Abdo Abamecha farms roughly 30 hectares in Badeyi, Limu Jimma at up to 2200 MASL — one of the higher plots in the region. The JARC varietals 74110 and 74112 grown here are known for clean floral expression, and this washed G1 lot delivers on that: white florals, stone fruit, and a dry black tea finish. Structured and precise without being austere. A straightforward filter coffee that doesn't ask much of you

name: Honduras Finca Gosen H-27 Anaerobic Natural
altitude: 1500 masl tasting notes : tropical fruits, cherry, raisin about the coffee : Mariano Nolasco farms Finca Gosen at 1500 MASL in La Pilas, a mountain community in Honduras where his family has worked the land for two generations. The H-27 varietal processed anaerobically — whole cherries fermented without oxygen — pushes the fruit forward in a way a standard natural won't. Expect tropical fruits, cherry, and raisin with real depth. Big, expressive, and built for filter

name: Kenya Thageini Lot 0424 CM Washed Diamond
altitude: 1750 masl tasting notes : roselle, blackcurrant, sugarcane about the coffee : Thageini wet mill sits within the Aguthi Farmers Cooperative in Nyeri, where around 450 smallholder members deliver cherry for collective processing. The CM washed method extends fermentation under controlled conditions, which pushes clarity and acidity without stripping body. SL28 and SL34 grown at this altitude tend toward bold fruit and firm structure, and that holds here. Expect roselle and blackcurrant upfront with a sugarcane sweetness that lingers and smooths the finish. Precise, expressive, and consistent across the cup

name: Peru Felipe Marin Mirez Geisha Natural La Palma
altitude: 1900 masl tasting notes : mango, hawthorn, milk chocolate about the coffee : Geisha from Peru are still rare, and Felipe Marin's lot from La Palma, Jaén earns the attention. At 1900 MASL, the Marin family farms alongside their father Silvestre, selecting cherries at peak ripeness and processing naturally at altitude. The result is precise and expressive: mango and hawthorn up front, with milk chocolate grounding the finish. It's a Geisha that doesn't overreach. Clean, sweet, and quietly confident

name: ROMA BLEND
altitude: clarity and sun-dried sweetness. This blend is a masterclass in balance, meticulously crafted to bridge the gap between the clean, crisp profiles of Central America and the wild, fruit-forward intensity of East Africa. The Composition We’ve paired two contrasting processes to create a multi-dimensional flavor profile: 50% Honduras (Washed Process): Provides the "spine" of the blend. The washed process ensures a clean, sparkling body and highlights the deep, chocolatey structure of the cacao notes. 50% Ethiopia (Natural Process): Adds the "soul" and sweetness. By drying the coffee cherry whole, we’ve preserved the intense sugars that translate into those unmistakable tropical and stone fruit characteristics. From the first sip, ROMA BLEND greets you with a bright, crystalline acidity reminiscent of starfruit . As the cup warms, it unfolds into a lush medley of tropical fruits —think mango and pineapple sweetness—all grounded by a sophisticated, velvet-like finish of cacao nibs . It is a vibrant, complex coffee that remains approachable whether brewed as a pour-over or a bright, modern espresso. Primary Notes : Starfruit, Tropical Fruits, Cacao Nibs Acidity : Bright & Citric Body : Medium, Silky
